title: Longest Special Path II
summary: Given an undirected tree rooted at node 0 with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, represented by a 2D array of edges where each edge connects two nodes and has a specified length, and an integer array nums where each element represents the value at the corresponding node, find the longest path from an ancestor node to a descendant node where all node values are distinct except for at most one value that may appear twice.
statement: Given an undirected tree rooted at node 0 with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, represented by a 2D array of edges where each edge connects two nodes and has a specified length, and an integer array nums where each element represents the value at the corresponding node, find the longest path from an ancestor node to a descendant node where all node values are distinct except for at most one value that may appear twice. Return an array of two values: the length of the longest special path and the minimum number of nodes in all possible longest special paths.
constraints: edges describes a positive-weight tree rooted at zero.
A valid downward ancestor-to-descendant path has all distinct values except that at most one value may occur twice.
Return [maximum total edge length, minimum node count among paths attaining that length].
hints: A window is valid after excluding all third occurrences and all but the largest active duplicate boundary.
During recursive DFS, maintain each value’s path occurrences plus Fenwick markers for penultimate and third-from-last depths.
Set the left boundary after the maximum third marker and after the second-largest penultimate marker; measure the prefix-distance span, then backtrack updates.
These two boundaries enforce frequency at most two and at most one duplicated value, while every ancestor window ending at each node is considered.
editorial: These two boundaries enforce frequency at most two and at most one duplicated value, while every ancestor window ending at each node is considered.

tests.explanation: The optimal special path has total length nine and uses three nodes.
One duplicated value is permitted, so the two-node path has length five.
